Hi Grace / Markus —

Thanks again for the overview earlier. We're very interested in the 'umbrella' demo you proposed that walks through latency, routing, and fallback behavior across US/EU/APAC.

Quick ask: our execs need a single 60-minute slot where our CEO (PST), our head of research in London, and our Japan engineering lead can all attend. The tricky part is DST shifting next week for our UK team. Can you propose a rotation or fallback if DST changes by a week?

I've copied Claire and Kenji to confirm availability windows from the UK and Japan side. Our preliminary windows (all in local times):
- PST: 08:00–11:30
- BST: 16:00–19:00
- JST: 00:00–03:00 (next day)

I know that's tight. If you can send a few concrete UTC options and call out the DST impact, that would help us lock a time.

Best,
Aiden
Quantify AI — Head of Partnerships

Subject: Re: Redwood demo — multi-region exec availability

Hi Aiden (and team),

Thanks — and appreciate the note about DST. Proposal below tries to make the overlap reasonable for each exec and also includes a plan if DST kicks in a week earlier/later than expected.

Candidate slots (all shown in UTC with local conversions in parentheses):
1) 15:00 UTC (PST 08:00 / BST 16:00 / JST 00:00+1) — earliest overlap; keeps US exec in morning
2) 17:00 UTC (PST 10:00 / BST 18:00 / JST 02:00+1) — slightly later for Japan but keeps London at end of day
3) 13:00 UTC (PST 06:00 / BST 14:00 / JST 22:00) — earlier for US; later for Japan but still doable for senior engineer in Tokyo

DST note: UK will switch from BST to GMT on 2028-08-20 in your calendar (we verified). If the meeting is scheduled after 2028-08-20 and the invite uses "Europe/London" the local time will drop by 1 hour. To avoid confusion we recommend:
- Option A: Send fixed UTC time in the invite (we set an explicit UTC time) and include local times in the body. That prevents calendar conversions from moving the slot.
- Option B: Use a rotating cadence — if you plan recurring demos across quarters, we can propose a round-robin schedule so no single region is always at a suboptimal hour.

I've attached a short mutual action plan (MAP_QA_v2.docx) with tasks and who from Quantify we should expect on the call.

Can you confirm which of the three slots works for your execs and whether you'd prefer Option A or Option B for handling DST? If none work, we'll propose two additional UTC-oriented times that avoid local-clock shifts.

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: MAP_QA_v2.docx
